zero_omission_notes.summary: Applies trigonometric ratios to measure real-world heights and distances using line of sight, angle of elevation, and angle of depression.

detailed_sections.section_number_and_title: 9.1 Line of Sight & Angles of Elevation / Depression
detailed_sections.full_explanation: Line of sight connects observer's eye to target. Angle of elevation is angle above horizontal line; angle of depression is angle below horizontal line.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Alternate Angles
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Angle of depression from top equals angle of elevation from ground.

procedure_or_steps: Measure distance d from tower base

diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Draw observer looking up at top and down at base relative to horizontal line.
diagrams_figures_and_maps.structural_or_conceptual_explanation: Standard layout for height and distance problems.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Relates object height h and distance d via tangent ratio.

textbook_exercises.question: Circus artist climbs 20 m rope tied from top of pole to ground at 30°. Find height of pole.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: A pole 6 m high casts shadow 2√3 m long. Sun's elevation is:

short_answer_questions.question: Ladder against wall makes 60° with ground. Foot is 2.5 m from wall. Find ladder length.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Angle of elevation of top of tower from two points at distances a and b from base are complementary. Prove height is √(ab).
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: tan θ = h/a and tan(90-θ) = cot θ = h/b. tan θ * cot θ = (h/a)*(h/b) = 1 => h^2/(ab) = 1 => h = √(ab).

comprehensive_long_answers.question: As observed from top of 75 m lighthouse, angles of depression of two ships are 30° and 45°. Find distance between ships.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Statue 1.6 m tall on top of pedestal. Angles of elevation of top of statue and top of pedestal are 60° and 45°.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Measuring angle of depression from vertical axis instead of horizontal baseline.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Always measure angle of depression downward from the horizontal baseline.
